verdict.rationale: incident.io documents deduplication keys that suppress new alerts while a matching alert is still active. It also documents alert grouping that merges related alerts into one group, so they are triaged, escalated and attached to an incident once. That directly delivers 'one incident pages one human, not fifty'. missing for 10: details on how grouping criteria and time windows are configured, and independent or hands-on corroboration of noise reduction.

support.subject: As an SRE, duplicate and related alerts are deduplicated and grouped so one incident pages one human, not fifty

citations.quote: if alert A is received with a deduplication key "x" and alert B with the same deduplication key is received while alert A is still active... no new alert will be created for alert B
a deduplication key is used to uniquely identify alerts and prevent the generation of duplicate alerts
Alert grouping groups those related alerts into a single alert group, so you can triage, escalate and attach them to an incident once
Group related alerts into an alert group so you can triage, escalate and attach them to incidents as one.
